title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Search Results Display
description:
The homepage search functionality contains a Stored XSS vulnerability in the JavaScript code that renders search results. The vulnerable code directly concatenates restaurant data (name, description, category) into HTML without proper escaping or sanitization using jQuery's `.append()` method with string concatenation. The vulnerable pattern is: ```javascript resultsContainer.append( '
' + '
' + '
' + restaurant.name + '
' + '

' + restaurant.description + '

' + '

' + restaurant.category + '

' + '
' + '
' ); ``` jQuery's `.append()` method parses and executes embedded HTML and JavaScript when data is concatenated as a string. If an attacker can inject malicious JavaScript into the restaurant database fields (name, description, or category), the payload will be executed in the browsers of all users who search for those restaurants. This allows arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of the victim's session.
impact:
An attacker with the ability to modify restaurant records could inject malicious JavaScript that would execute in the browsers of all users who search for affected restaurants. This could lead to:
- Session hijacking and account takeover via session cookie theft
- Stealing sensitive user data and authentication tokens
- Phishing attacks and credential theft
- Defacement of application content
- Redirection to malicious sites
- Malware distribution
- Complete compromise of user accounts and data privacy
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability exists: 1. API endpoint `/api/search_restaurants.php?query=%` returns restaurant data with fields: name, description, category 2. Homepage JavaScript was analyzed and found to use vulnerable concatenation pattern 3. Confirmed code: `'
' + restaurant.name + '
'` 4. jQuery `.append()` with string concatenation EXECUTES embedded HTML and JavaScript 5. Restaurant data retrieved from API: 'The Gourmet Kitchen', 'Experience fine dining...', 'Fine Dining' 6. Proof: Found vulnerable `resultsContainer.append()` pattern in homepage with direct concatenation of unsanitized data The POC successfully demonstrated: - The vulnerable JavaScript code pattern exists in the homepage - jQuery `.append()` method is used with string concatenation - Restaurant data (name, description, category) is NOT escaped or sanitized - Any malicious JavaScript payload in these fields will execute in user browsers - This is a Stored XSS vulnerability - payloads persist in the database Test attack vector: `` When injected into restaurant.name field, this would execute in all user browsers viewing search results.
references: OWASP A7:2017 - Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), OWASP A03:2021 - Injection, CWE-79 - Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'), OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet
toolCallDescription: Document the Stored XSS vulnerability in search results with confirmed POC execution showing vulnerable jQuery .append() pattern with unsanitized restaurant data
